messages:
infra-bot: ALERT: paging oncall @maria — increased 5xx (504/502) observed from inference-gateway in prod-private-vpc (customer CUST-42). start=2026-03-15T12:13:02Z, 5m error rate=32%, top path=/v1/generate

maria (oncall): ack, I'm on it. looking at metrics and traces now. initial hypothesis: NAT translation pressure or SG causing intermittent drops.

ben: pinging the gw host now. if it's NAT ephemeral exhaustion we should see conntrack counts high. can you run `sudo conntrack -L | wc -l` and `ss -s`?

maria (oncall): running:
```
maria (oncall): sudo conntrack -L | wc -l
maria (oncall): 198420

maria (oncall): ss -s
maria (oncall): TCP:   145000 (estab 1200, closed 1200, orphaned 0)
```

lee: conntrack at ~198k — that's close to the default 196608 on these appliances. could be hitting limit and dropping new sessions => 504s upstream.

ops-sre: also seeing a burst of SYN_RECV and RST on the transit interface. adding to suspicion it's ephemeral exhaustion.

customer-support: Customer CUST-42 reports timeouts from their inference calls since ~12:10 UTC, production traffic only. Any ETA we can tell them?

maria (oncall): short mitigation: enable short-lived ephemeral port range expansion and increase conntrack_max on the gateway. I'm going to apply temporary bump and route small percentage to fallback pool. calling it out before change: applying sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=500000 on gateway nodes and expanding ephemeral ports to 30000-61000.

ben: +1 — prepare rollback steps. Also opening quick firewall check: `aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces` to ensure SGs not being reapplied by autoscaling hooks.

maria (oncall): applying now (patching one host at a time):
```
maria (oncall): for node in gw-az1-0 gw-az1-1; do ssh $node "sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=500000 && sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range=30000 61000"; done
```

infra-bot: DEPLOYMENT: sysctl change scheduled on gw-az1-0. runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/nat-conntrack-bump

maria (oncall): done on gw-az1-0. metrics show conntrack dropped from 198k -> 62k on that host and 5xx rate on that host's traffic decreased from 40% -> 4% within 30s.

ben: replicating to gw-az1-1 now. also shifting 20% of CUST-42 traffic to fallback pool (region-b) via smart-routing override to reduce pressure while we stabilize.

deploy-bot: ROUTE-CHANGE: traffic shift 20% -> region-b applied (id: rchg-20260315-01).

maria (oncall): after second node patch, global 5m error rate for the customer down to 6%. still seeing occasional gateway 504s on a subset of hosts — investigating whether any host-level SG re-applied by autoscaling lifecycle hooks.

lee: checked autoscaling lifecycle hooks logs, there's a cron job that runs a tagging script that re-applies a baseline SG for compliance. it runs every 5 minutes and just touched gw-az2-0 at 12:12 UTC; change was a noop but re-application briefly closed some ephemeral entries.

ops-sre: that's likely the final needle — repeated SG reapply causes conntrack churn which combined with high session counts leads to errors. we should throttle that script or add a guard to skip when conntrack high.

maria (oncall): agreed. immediate next step: disable the SG-reapply cron on the gateway fleet (non-compliance risk acknowledged) and keep fallback routing until overnight maintenance. will coordinate with security for a postmortem.

customer-support: pls update CUST-42: told them we applied temporary fixes (conntrack bump, expanded port range, routed some traffic to fallback) and errors are down to normal. they asked for RCA and ETA on permanent fix.

ben: permanent fixes: 1) increase conntrack limit in AMI and bake, 2) adjust autoscaling lifecycle hook to avoid SG reapply or make it stateless, 3) add proactive conntrack alerts tied to error budget, 4) consider NAT load-spread across more gateways.

infra-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: mitigation applied. severity: P2 (customer-impacting degradation). ticket created: INC-20260315-4213.

maria (oncall): handing off to ben for longtail remediation and customer comms. I'm going offline for a break, @ben wants handoff?

ben: taking over. oncall-handoff: @maria -> @ben at 2026-03-15T12:45:00Z. I'll coordinate with security and infra to schedule the AMI bake and lifecycle hook rollback. leaving routing override in place until confirmed stable.

ops-sre: recommend a short postmortem with timeline, root cause (conntrack + SG reapply), and action items. tagging @security.

customer-support: thanks. I'll send the customer a summary and ETA for full remediation (target 48 hours). they appreciate the fast mitigation.

ben: logging final notes: root cause: conntrack exhaustion exacerbated by periodic SG reapply causing session churn. mitigation: bumped conntrack_max, expanded ephemeral port range, shifted traffic to fallback pool, disabled SG cron. next: bake AMI with higher defaults, add conntrack alerts, throttle lifecycle hook.

infra-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (mitigations in place). see ticket INC-20260315-4213 for action items and postmortem schedule.
